You look, and leave it. That number grows by itself.

lines.text: v15 you wrote last week, v16 is Vivi's edit, the boss wants v17. One page at a time: his words above, the two versions below, you choose which side stays, I render it.
Snapshot taken; this one will not change again. Hand it to the boss, he will read it out as is.
Sent to the boss. He will look at it sooner or later.

bubbles: The foundation page needs more 【weight】. An investor should hear at once that we are 【not a wrapper】, not a skin on somebody else's model put up for sale.
This version is still 【missing something】: the numbers are fine, the presence isn't. Think it over. I won't rewrite it for you; work it out yourself.
No rush, just send it before you leave. Once this page is right the whole story stands up. Lay the foundation first, the rest later.

remark.c1: Two hundred and eleven nodes. Xiao Zhang counted twice. The boss never counted once.
remark.d1: The model is rented. Write 'our own' on the page; the rent is still due.

bubbles: The data part has to show a 【closed loop】: data comes in, the model improves, the client sends more data, round it goes. Investors love that circle.
Using 【real-time】 twice does no harm. 'Imported once a week' is the kind of sentence you already know not to put on a page.
Don't go too fine on the granularity; the direction is what matters. What do you think? I think you already know, you just don't dare write it.

remark.c2: Three clients' spreadsheets, imported weekly. Not one word in that sentence excites anyone.
remark.d3: Imported weekly. Call it real time if you like. Real time, once a week.

bubbles: Don't oversell the AI part. What investors fear most right now is 'fully automatic'; who takes the fall is their first question. 【A person in the loop】.
This page can be a little more down to earth: just what we actually do every day. Don't reach too high here; keep the height for the later pages.
Look at how the competitors write it, but keep our own character. They say fully automatic; we say a person checks. Go the other way.

remark.c3: He said this himself at 08:58 this morning. I have it recorded.
remark.d2: Fully automatic means nobody checks. When an investor asks who checks, what do you say.

bubbles: Stop writing 【moat】. Every deck has a moat; a judge doesn't even look up at the word. Write something 【concrete】, something with a picture in it.
The story should be sexier. But sexy is not a pile of adjectives, it is detail: one number, one thing, beats ten adjectives.
Open up your perspective, think from the company's side. 'Three years of experience' — the company is two years old. Don't hand anyone a stick.

remark.c4: Two hundred-odd nodes matched one by one. Truly hard to copy: too slow.
remark.d4: Three years of experience. The company is two.

bubbles: Numbers should leave 【room for imagination】. Two clients is a fact, but facts are for private briefings, not for the page.
On the clients page I'm not asking you to lie, but you have to know how to use 【leading】. 'Served' and 'signed' are two different things, you know that.
The direction is fine; polish the details. Drop the 'paid' column for now; investors want momentum, not accounting vouchers.

remark.c5: Two pilots, one has paid. An investor will ask where the second one is.
remark.d5: Fifty. One has paid; forty-nine live in the imagination.

note: What the boss said is far too vague: a riddler through and through.
Maybe some things he said before can help?
launch.call: Use the boss's riddle-like feedback to find the answer that satisfies him (though he never says it)!
